definitions.gloss: imperial court, the emperor and his government
definitions.explanation: The court of the emperor, including the emperor himself and the officials who governed under his authority. Primarily used in historical contexts to refer to the seat of imperial governance in Japan, particularly before the Meiji Restoration.

examples.japanese: {朝廷|ちょうてい}に{仕|つか}える。
{朝廷|ちょうてい}と{幕府|ばくふ}の{関係|かんけい}は{複雑|ふくざつ}だった。
examples.english: The relationship between the imperial court and the shogunate was complicated.

examples.japanese: {平安時代|へいあんじだい}の{朝廷|ちょうてい}では、{貴族|きぞく}たちが{政治|せいじ}の{実権|じっけん}を{握|にぎ}っていた。
examples.english: In the imperial court of the Heian period, the aristocrats held real political power.

notes:
USAGE:
{朝廷|ちょうてい} refers to the Japanese imperial court as a governing institution. It is a historical term encountered primarily when studying or discussing pre-modern Japanese history, literature, and culture.

During the feudal period, power was divided between the {朝廷|ちょうてい} (imperial court) in Kyoto and the {幕府|ばくふ} (shogunate). The court retained ceremonial and symbolic authority while real political power shifted to the military government.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {朝廷|ちょうてい}に{仕|つか}える: to serve the court
- {朝廷|ちょうてい}と{幕府|ばくふ}: court and shogunate
- {朝廷|ちょうてい}の{権威|けんい}: authority of the court
- {朝廷|ちょうてい}{政治|せいじ}: court politics
